summary.headline: Celemics: Largest shareholder Park Jong-gap pledges 487,425 shares as collateral for KRW 3.5bn loan
summary.what_happened: On Nov 26, 2026, Celemics filed a corrected report on a share pledge agreement involving its largest shareholder, Park Jong-gap, who pledged part of his holdings as collateral and guarantor for a loan taken by G&M Co., Ltd. The collateral type was changed from an assignment of collateral to a pledge (질권) on Nov 17, 2026, and the creditor changed following a refinancing of existing debt on Oct 13, 2026. Park retains voting rights over the pledged shares during the pledge period.

key_numbers.label: Largest shareholder's holding at filing date
Holding if all pledged shares were enforced

summary.why_it_matters: In Korea, share pledges by major shareholders are disclosed because, if the loan defaults and the pledge is enforced, the pledged shares could be transferred to the creditor, potentially changing the largest shareholder's stake and control. Investors typically watch the size of pledged shares relative to holdings and the price levels that trigger enforcement.
